results.name: family_leeds_budget
results.reply: With family weighting applied, **Garforth East** leads (75.7) on safety (74.8) and transport (91.8) at a £305k median — the safest pick on this list for young kids. **Meanwood** (71.9) and **Far Headingley & Weetwood** (71.7) score higher on education and amenities but trade off some safety. The western areas like Guiseley and Otley are cheap (£275k) with excellent transport links but their safety scores drop into the 40s–50s, so worth a closer look at specific streets if you're considering them. Want me to compare a few in detail or check schools and nurseries near a particular one?

results.name: commuter_manchester
results.reply: The top picks are heavily in Trafford and Stockport — Sale Central, Timperley and Altrincham East all score near-perfect on transport (fast Metrolink/tram links to the city centre) and amenities, which is exactly what a daily commuter needs. The main trade-off is affordability: every top-10 area scores below 50 on housing, with Sale Central the standout value at a £255k median versus £500k+ in Timperley. If budget matters, Sale Central or Sale North are the best balance; if you want a more residential feel and can stretch, West Timperley or Bramhall West add safety and community on top.

results.name: retiree_devon
results.reply: I've weighted for safety, quiet environment and health services (retiree preset). The top results are all from **North Devon** — Barnstaple Pilton leads on a blend of very good environment (90), health access (89) and reasonable safety (59), with a median price around £227k. Fremington & Instow scores best on safety (84) but is quieter on amenities. Would you like me to widen the search to Exeter, Torquay or other parts of Devon?

results.name: safest_bristol
results.reply: Weighted heavily on safety, the top of the list is led by **Downend North** (safety 82) and **Westbury-on-Trym** (safety 70) — the latter being the safest neighbourhood within Bristol city boundaries. Henleaze (60) and Westbury Park (59) follow, both in Clifton/Clifton Hill area. The trade-off is affordability: the safest Bristol areas (Westbury-on-Trym, Henleaze) have very low housing scores, while the more affordable South Glos neighbours (Downend, Emersons Green) are also safer but technically outside the city. Want me to zoom into one of these?

results.name: brighton_street_level_budget
results.reply: Eight LSOAs qualify, all within 10 km of Brighton. Want me to profile any of these in more detail or adjust the criteria?

results.name: young_professional_london
results.reply: The young-professional weighting (heavy on transport, nightlife and pubs) puts a cluster of South and East London areas at the top. Millwall South, Leamouth and Rotherhithe all score above 76 with near-perfect transport and amenities while staying around £440–530k — a big value gap versus Merton Road and Clapham Common West, which add polish but push £730k–£905k. Safety scores dip in the river-side areas (40–50), which is the main trade-off to weigh. Want me to dig into any of these or narrow by budget?

results.name: profile_postcode
results.reply: LS6 3AA is in **Headingley, Leeds** (LSOA E01011440), scoring 68.9 overall — 73rd percentile nationally. Its standout features are excellent amenities (99th percentile for sports, food & drink and supermarkets) and transport (98.6, with gigabit broadband and a station ~920 m away), but safety is a major drag at 10.7 (4th percentile), driven by high burglary, theft/vehicle crime and road collisions. The typical house price of ~£219k is flagged as an estimate based on few recent sales, steadied toward the surrounding area.

results.name: profile_place
results.reply:
Whitley Bay Promenade (North Tyneside 006A) sits at the 61st percentile nationally, but the picture is polarised. It excels on environment (96th percentile), transport (96th), amenities (97th) and health services (95th) — you're 400 m from the station with clean air and no flood risk. The drag is safety: violent and sexual offences are around 104 per 1,000 residents a year, putting the area in the bottom 3rd percentile nationally. Housing condition is also very poor, and community & wellbeing is weak, so the overall score masks a trade-off between an attractive location and a rougher daily environment.

If safety is a priority for you, I can reweight the index or rank nearby North East alternatives to see what balances well.

results.name: compare_two
results.reply: Chapel Allerton North edges ahead overall (73 vs 71), pulling ahead on safety, schools and community, while Headingley is the clear winner for transport and amenities — a more connected, sociable area with more well-run pubs. Chapel Allerton is quieter (about half the density) with less burglary but pricier homes; Headingley offers more value on house prices. The choice really comes down to whether you prioritise a calmer, family-oriented feel or a more vibrant, amenity-rich setting.

results.name: compare_three_bristol
results.reply: All three are top-decile neighbourhoods (97th+ percentile for Redland and Clifton; 79th for Bedminster), with similar strengths in environment, health and transport. The main trade-offs: **Redland** is the safest (65.6 vs 38 and 42) but the priciest at ~£447k; **Clifton East** leads on schools (87.7) and community (94.1) at a more moderate ~£384k; **Bedminster** is the most affordable of the three but carries notably more violent crime (24.8 per 1,000 vs 10–18) and a lower community score. If schools or community life matter most, Clifton East looks like the sweet spot; if safety is the priority, Redland wins at a premium.

results.name: well_run_pubs
results.reply: Eight well-run pubs within half a mile, all with a top hygiene rating of 5. The closest is The Phoenix at ~260 m, followed by Cask & Glass and The Pineapple, all on the south side of the area. Bbar (346 m) is the only one flagged as having outdoor seating. Distances are straight-line.

results.name: nearest_gp
results.reply: The closest are **New Islington Medical Centre** and **Ancoats Urban Village Medical Practice** (both at M4 6EE), roughly 770 m straight-line. **City Health Centre** on M1 1PL is a similar distance if you prefer something in the same postcode district.

results.name: explain_safety_gmp
results.reply: The safety score is dragged down mainly by a high rate of violent and sexual offences (the weakest indicator), with criminal damage and public order also pulling it down; road danger is actually very low. The big caveat is that these rates use residents as the denominator, so a busy town centre with few residents and many visitors is penalised — and Greater Manchester's figures are estimated rather than official. So treat this as partly an artefact of how a dense, visit-heavy area is measured.

results.name: explain_high_score
results.reply:
It's actually not that high — 67.3 is the 66th percentile, above median but far from the top. What pushes it up is a near-perfect amenities score (parks, shops, culture, well-run pubs all max out) and an excellent transport score (station 147 m away, 21 buses an hour, gigabit broadband). Strong school quality and close access to a GP, dentist and pharmacy add further.

The two themes that hold it back are safety (18.5, dragged down by very high burglary and anti-social behaviour rates) and housing affordability (15.3, with a typical price around £1.39 m). So the "high" score really reflects Hampstead's walkability, green space and local services rather than safety or affordability.

results.name: what_is_measured_schools
results.reply: This theme covers school performance (inspection outcomes and attainment), capacity and wait times for nurseries and pre-school places, and the availability of secondary schools within a reasonable distance. The inspection data is benchmarked within each nation since England, Wales and other regions use different frameworks.

results.name: compare_top_two_followup

Far Headingley & Weetwood makes up for that with noticeably better local amenities (84.9 vs 60.8) and slightly better schools — so the trade-off is essentially a quieter, safer suburb versus a more village-like high street with more on offer locally.

results.name: crime_rate_question
results.reply: Hanover's safety score is 59.9 (63rd percentile nationally) — moderate overall. The headline figure is 14.4 violent and sexual offences per 1,000 residents a year, which actually scores well (80.4) against the national benchmark; the real drag is road safety, with 6.8 serious collisions per year within 500 m scoring just 1.8. So while personal crime isn't the issue, road danger is this area's standout safety weakness.

results.name: house_price_question
results.reply: The typical house price in Central Harrogate is **£271,100**, which sits in the 58th percentile for England — above the national median of £51.5k score-wise but still relatively affordable given the town's strong amenities and transport scores. The council tax figure (Band D, £2,544/yr) is a council-wide average rather than a local estimate, so treat it as approximate.

results.name: analyst_sql
results.reply: Kingston upon Hull leads at 99.9% average gigabit availability across its 168 neighbourhoods, followed by Oadby & Wigston (98.8%) and Luton (98.7%).
